items.rationale: The model has no memory between calls; the program resends the setup plus all earlier requests and results every time. Answer a believes the model remembers by itself (M3), and c ignores that results must be sent back for the model to use them.

A new session starts with an empty window, so the fact must be saved outside it and loaded back. A larger window does not carry anything over (M7), a system prompt cannot hold facts the model has never been given (M3), and resending all chats is huge, costly and noisy.

Call 1 input 1,000. Call 2 input 1,000 + 50 + 200 = 1,250. Call 3 input 1,250 + 50 + 800 = 2,100. Total 1,000 + 1,250 + 2,100 = 4,350. A wrong answer of 2,100 gives only the final context size and forgets that every call is billed separately.

items.answer: The chunk does not say which machine or material it belongs to, so search cannot tell; add a short note on its source (machine and section) to each chunk before indexing.
accepted: It lost its context when split from the manual; prepend the machine and section to each chunk before indexing.
The chunk does not name the machine, so it matches any machine; label each chunk with its machine and section.
items.rationale: Full credit needs the cause (the chunk is ambiguous alone because the surrounding context was lost) and a fix (add source context to each chunk before indexing). One half only is partial. Blaming the model size or window is wrong (M8 is the idea that a chunk means the same alone as in the manual).

items.answer: Compact: summarize the conversation and continue in a fresh window; the risk is that the summary is lossy and drops details.
accepted: Clear old tool results; the risk is losing information the model may still need.
Save notes to storage outside the window and reload them; the cost is deciding what to write, and missing notes mean lost facts.
Summarize earlier steps and restart with the summary; details may be lost.
items.rationale: Any one of compaction, clearing old tool results or writing notes outside the window is right, with a correct cost: lost detail or extra work. Naming a method with no cost or risk is partial. Answering that a bigger window removes the problem ignores context rot and cost (M7).
